Can you explain the main options in simple terms?
Absolutely! Here's a simple breakdown of the main spirit categories:
Whiskey (the big family)
This is the umbrella term for spirits made from grains and aged in barrels. All whiskeys share this basic process, but where they're made and how they're produced creates different styles.
Bourbon
America's native whiskey, must be made with at least 51% corn
Sweeter and smoother than other whiskeys, with vanilla and caramel notes
No added flavoring allowed — just water and the natural barrel aging
Great for beginners because of its approachable sweetness
Scotch
Whiskey made in Scotland
Often has smoky, peaty flavors (though not always)
All Scotch is whiskey, but not all whiskey is Scotch
Tends to be more complex and varied in flavor
Tequila
Made from blue agave plants in Mexico
Ranges from fresh and citrusy (blanco) to rich and smooth (añejo)
Completely different flavor profile from whiskey
Rum
Made from sugarcane or molasses
Sweet, tropical flavors
Ranges from light and crisp to dark and rich
Vodka & Gin
Vodka: neutral, clean spirit — great for cocktails
Gin: vodka infused with botanicals (juniper, herbs, spices)
We carry over 20,000 spirits across all these categories, from well-known classics to rare finds.

Is there anything else a beginner needs to get started?
• Just now
Seen • Just now
Good question! The great news is you don't need much to get started. Here's what will help you enjoy bourbon properly:
What you'll need:
1. A proper glass (optional but recommended)
The best glass for tasting bourbon is a Glencairn or tulip-shaped glass — it concentrates the aromas toward your nose and delivers the ultimate tasting experience. If you don't have one, any whiskey tumbler works perfectly fine.
2. Water (essential)
Have plenty of water on hand to alternate sips and clear your palate. Adding a few drops of water to your bourbon can actually release flavors and soften the alcohol punch. Use spring water or soft tap water that won't add its own flavor.
3. Ice (optional)
If you prefer bourbon "on the rocks," use big cubes or spheres — they melt slower so the bourbon gets chilled but less watered down.
How to drink it:
Neat (no ice, no water) — best for exploring all the flavors
On the rocks (over ice) — refreshing and smooth
With a splash of water — opens up the flavors
Bottom line: You really just need the bourbon itself and some water. A good glass enhances the experience, but isn't required to start.

How do I use it properly the very first time?
• Just now
Seen • Just now
Great question! Here's your step-by-step guide for your first bourbon tasting:
Step 1: Pour & Prepare
Pour a small amount (about 1-2 ounces) into your glass. Start neat (no ice, no water) to experience the full flavor profile. Have water nearby to sip between tastings.
Step 2: Look
Give it a little swirl and admire the color and "legs" (the liquid cascading down the glass).
Step 3: Smell (The Most Important Part!)
Gently bring the glass up to your nose — don't rush this step! You don't want to overwhelm your nose. Tilt the glass to one side and really get your nose in there.
Take your nose away after each sniff, then repeat. The first thing you smell is usually accurate, then other layers will slowly reveal themselves. With Penelope Classic, you should notice butterscotch, vanilla, and candied orange.
Step 4: Taste
Take a small sip and roll the bourbon over your tongue and around its sides, then throughout your mouth. Savor the flavors and start identifying them. Look for brown sugar, honeyed corn, and cinnamon notes.
Step 5: Experiment
After tasting it neat, try adding a few drops of water — this can actually release more flavors and soften the alcohol.
Pro tip: Don't feel pressured to finish it quickly. Take breaks, sip water, and enjoy the experience!
